tasks.name: HttpClient Protocol, Response, and HttpxClient returning CliResult[Response]
inputs: spec Why a Protocol for HttpClient
docs/api-notes.md Cloudflare bot management (the verification result)
AGENTS.md Functional core / imperative shell rule (Protocol and Response are core, HttpxClient is shell)
tasks.description: src/inso_dumper/http/client.py defines BROWSER_LIKE_HEADERS (the exact dict from the spec: User-Agent, Accept, Accept-Language: pl-PL, Accept-Encoding, sec-ch-ua, sec-ch-ua-mobile, sec-ch-ua-platform, Upgrade-Insecure-Requests) as a module-level Mapping[str, str] with MappingProxyType to enforce immutability at runtime. Define the HttpClient Protocol (async def request(method, path, *, form=None, headers=None) -> CliResult[Response]) — the Protocol's return type is CliResult[Response], not raw Response, so the contract says what the shell really delivers. Define a @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) class Response (status: int, body: bytes, headers: Sequence[tuple[str, str]] preserving duplicate Set-Cookie entries, text() returning the decoded body) — pure data. Implement HttpxClient(Config) whose request merges BROWSER_LIKE_HEADERS with caller headers, applies the per-host rate limit, sends the request, and on any httpx.HTTPError / OSError returns Err(CliError(HTTP, subject=...)) immediately. A non-2xx status is not an error at this layer — it's a Response(status=4xx, ...) that the caller (parser or shell) interprets. The v1 client does not follow redirects automatically so the login's 302 chain is observable by the caller; the shell's login function (T7) follows them. There is no HttpxClientError exception type — the boundary is Result, not raise-then-catch.

tasks.name: Pure login payload + response parser, and the login shell
inputs: docs/api-notes.md Auth model and the spike's login HAR (entry 41: form-encoded body, 302 response with Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID=...)

tasks.description: src/inso_dumper/http/auth.py provides two pure functions: build_login_payload(email: str, password: str) -> Mapping[str, str] returning {'_username': email, '_password': password}, and parse_login_response(response: Response) -> CliResult[Session] that takes the final Response from the redirect chain (the shell chose where to stop) and extracts Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID=<opaque>; ... from response.headers (a Sequence[tuple[str, str]] so duplicate Set-Cookie entries are preserved) and the user_uuid from the response's URL (or, if the shell didn't capture it, the parser accepts a final_url: str parameter as a fallback). Missing PHPSESSID or missing UUID returns Err(CliError(kind=AUTH, subject=...)). The shell function login(client: HttpClient, config: Config, email: str, password: str) -> CliResult[Session] lives in src/inso_dumper/http/login.py: GET /login (warm-up), POST /login with the payload, follow redirects until the URL matches /panel/home/<uuid>/ or the chain length exceeds a small cap (5 hops), call parse_login_response on the final response, return the result. The shell never raises; any CliResult[Response, CliError] returned by client.request is chained via match (with case Ok(r): continue; case Err(e): return Err(e)) so the shell's return type is the propagated CliResult[Session]. The single try/except in this module catches httpx.HTTPError / OSError and converts to Err(CliError(HTTP, subject)) immediately per the AGENTS.md rule.

tasks.name: typer app, exit-code dispatcher, README, and the Phase 1 plan.md check
inputs: spec Error handling approach (the exit_code_for sketch)
AGENTS.md Functional core / imperative shell rule (the single outer try/except rule)
tasks.description: src/inso_dumper/cli.py defines the typer app: login (read INSO_EMAIL / INSO_PASSWORD, build HttpxClient, call login shell from T7, save_session), children (orchestrate T8), --version (from pyproject.toml via importlib.metadata.version), --help. The exit_code_for function from the spec is implemented and used by both commands to map the final CliError to the documented exit code via match + assert_never. The single outer try/except Exception in cli.py is the last-resort safety net: it catches anything that escaped the result-typed boundary (programmer error, library bug), logs at ERROR via the redaction filter, and returns exit 99 (INTERNAL). This is the only place an uncaught Exception is allowed, and AGENTS.md names it explicitly. src/inso_dumper/__main__.py re-exports the typer app for 'python -m inso_dumper'. The validate entry from python-build-tools (ruff format --check, ruff check, basedpyright, pytest -q) must pass before declaring T9 done. A short README.md documents the two commands, the env vars, the session file location, and the exit codes.
